declarations.proved_scope: Rational view sends an embedded integer to the same rational integer.
The map from Z[1/D] to Q is injective for D>0.
Eligible reduction sends embedded integers to their target-ring casts.
The localized fraction times its denominator equals its numerator.
The rational view of a localized fraction equals its actual rational value.
The finite product of rational denominators is positive.
Each denominator divides the finite denominator product.
Every entry in any finite rational table is exactly represented in Z[1/D].
Storing a nonzero rational reciprocal makes the original absolute numerator divide D.
Coprimality of D and p makes D a unit modulo p^f for every f.
An odd eligible prime exists for every positive finite denominator product, uniformly for every f.
Rationally zero localized coefficients reduce to zero.
Rational lower-triangular zero patterns survive reduction.
Entrywise rational view is injective on square localized matrices.
Rational matrix equality reflects to the localization and survives eligible reduction.
Rational matrix product identities survive eligible reduction.
Rational projector idempotence implies actual reduced projector idempotence.
Both rational nested absorption equations survive eligible reduction.
Reduction preserves projector complements.
Reduction preserves matrix differences.
Exact three-factor rational matrix identities survive reduction with the same factors.
A stored integral pattern reduces to its ordinary integer-cast pattern.
Reduction commutes with Kronecker products, including rectangular matrices.
Stored rational two-sided inverses remain two-sided inverses in the target ring.
A rational right-inverse table implies unit determinant for the reduced minor.
A nonzero rational determinant and its stored exact inverse imply a reduced unit determinant.
A rational scalar inverse witness implies the reduced scalar is a unit.
A finite table containing a nonzero entry and its reciprocal preserves its unit status.
The actual prime-power address gauge constructed from rational idempotence is involutive.
The matrix action on coordinate vectors preserves subtraction.
Prime-power nested partial-swap transport follows from rational absorption and coprimality, with no reduced-identity premise.
